money.title: Money as integers
money.text: Every amount is an `i64` in the smallest unit of `APP_CURRENCY` (cents with `USD`; `INTEGER` on SQLite, `BIGINT` on PostgreSQL), never a float: `0.1 + 0.2` isn't `0.3` in floating point, and a sum of prices must be exact. Templates show it with the `money` filter; fees are worked out in basis points with integer rounding (`staff::model::fee`).

encrypted.title: Secrets: Encrypted
encrypted.text: A customer's ID number (needed to rent a bike) is an `Encrypted<String>`: sealed with `APP_KEY` when it's written, so the `customers.id_number` column holds unreadable text and a stolen database leaks nothing. The app reads the plain value; the field is `#[serde(skip_serializing)]`, so it never reaches a template or an API answer by accident, and staff see `masked_id_number()`.

enums.title: Statuses: DbEnum
enums.text: Every status and kind is a Rust enum with `#[derive(DbEnum)]`: stored as a word (`overdue`, `waiting_parts`), read back as the enum, so a typo is a compile error and a form sending an unknown value gets a validation error.

soft_deletes.title: Soft deletes
soft_deletes.text: Customers who leave and discontinued products are **soft deleted** (`#[model(soft_deletes)]`, a `deleted_at` column): queries skip them, `restore` brings them back, and the rentals, orders and payments that point at them keep working. Everything else is history that is never deleted: a rental is returned or cancelled, an order refunded.

seed.title: Factories and the seeders
seed.text:
Every model has a `Factory` in its area's `factories.rs`, with states and sequences named after the business: `rentals().of_bike(&bike).overdue()`, `rental_bikes().owned_by(north).placed_at(south)`, `orders().at(store).paid()`, `work_orders().waiting_parts()`. Tests make exactly the rows they need with them (`seed::fixtures` adds stores and people with roles).

`cargo run -- db:seed` builds a small shop in a second; `cargo run -- demo:seed --size large` builds Pagila's volume (about 1,000 variants, 600 customers, 16,000 rentals, 5,000 orders, 3,000 work orders) in a few seconds. The dates count back from today, so the shop is always alive: rentals out and overdue, one due back later today, work on the bench, low stock, bikes and goods at other stores, someone helping another store this week, last month's balances still open. A seed never runs twice: `db:seed` skips a seeded database and `demo:seed` refuses it.

access.title: Who may do what: RBAC + ABAC
access.lead: Roles say what, stores say where.
access.text: The code checks **permissions** (`access::catalogue`), never a role's name: a role is a named set of permissions that the owner can change without a deploy. Roles are given **in a store** (`assign_role_in(…, &Scope::of(&store))`), optionally between two dates (staff helping another store), and only the owner's role is global. On the staff side a middleware picks the store the request works in and calls `permissions::set_scope`, so `require_permission`, `allows` and `can()` count the roles in that store; another store's record answers 404.

about.title: The JSON API
about.lead: Every endpoint for the store kiosks and the shop's app: what it needs, what to send, what comes back.
about.rule_token: Send a token as Authorization: Bearer; without one the answer is 401, without the endpoint's ability 403.
about.rule_errors: A refused request is 422 {"message", "errors"}, with the same rules as the website; lists come in pages with links.
about.rule_limit: :count requests a minute per token; over that, 429 with Retry-After.
